{{Short description|none}} {{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox Hurling All-Ireland| |year=2002 |image= |dates= 27 April - 8 September 2002 |teams = 21 |team1= Kilkenny |titles= 27th |captain1= [[Andy Comerford]] |manager1= [[Brian Cody]] |team2= Clare |captain2= [[Brian Lohan]] |manager2= [[Cyril Lyons]] |munster= Waterford |leinster= Kilkenny |ulster= Antrim |connacht= |matches= 30 |totalgoals= |totalpoints= |topscorer= [[File: Colours of Tipperary.svg|border|20px]] [[Eoin Kelly (Tipperary hurler)|Eoin Kelly]] (2–39) |poty= [[File: Colours of Kilkenny.svg|border|20px]] [[Henry Shefflin]] |previous=[[2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2001]] |next = [[2003 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|2003]] }} The '''2002 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' (known as the '''[[Guinness]] Hurling Championship''' for sponsorship reasons) was the 116th staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] since its establishment by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] in 1887. The draws for the respective provincial championships took place on 27 October 2001.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/gaelic-football/unfair-provincial-format-should-draw-its-last-breath/26072727.html|title=Unfair provincial format should draw its last breath|date=31 October 2001|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=17 May 2023|first=Martin|last=Breheny}} The championship ran from 27 April to 8 September 2002. [[Tipperary GAA|Tipperary]] entered the championship as the [[2001 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|defending champions]], however, they were beaten by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[#All-Ireland semi-finals|All-Ireland semi-final]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/carey-proves-that-class-is-permanent-in-croker-epic/26038203.html|title=Carey proves that class is permanent in Croker epic|date=19 August 2002|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=17 May 2023|first=|last=}} The [[2002 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|All-Ireland final]] was played on 8 September 2002 at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]], between Kilkenny and [[Clare GAA|Clare]], in what was their fourth championship meeting overall but their first All-Ireland final meeting in [[1932 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship final|70 years]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/cody-at-odds-with-the-odds/26038319.html|title=Cody at odds with the odds|date=20 August 2002|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=17 May 2023|first=Martin|last=Breheny}} Kilkenny won the match by 2–20 to 0–19 to claim their 27th All-Ireland title overall and a first title in [[2000 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|two years]].{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/classy-cats-cream-clare/26033889.html|title=Classy Cats cream Clare|date=9 September 2002|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=17 May 2023|first=|last=}}{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-30067466.html|title=Cats tear Bannermen apart|date=8 September 2002|publisher=Irish Examiner|access-date=17 May 2023|first=|last=}} Tipperary's [[Eoin Kelly (Tipperary hurler)|Eoin Kelly]] was the championship's [[#Top scorers|top scorer]] with 2–39.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/news/eoin-is-top-championship/27449097.html|title=Eoin is top championship scorer|date=12 September 2002|publisher=Irish Independent|access-date=17 May 2023|first=|last=}} == Teams == === General information === Twenty one counties will compete in the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]]: one team in the [[Connacht Senior Hurling Championship]], ten teams in the [[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]], five teams in the [[Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] and five teams in the [[Ulster Senior Hurling Championship]]. {| |[[File:Colours_of_Wicklow.svg|border|20x20px]] [[Wicklow GAA|Wicklow]] | – | – |First preliminary round ([[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]]) |} ===All-Ireland final=== The new Qualifier system threw up an interesting pairing in the All-Ireland final. It was the [[Leinster]] champions [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] versus [[Clare GAA|Clare]], who were knocked out of the provincial championship in the very first round. Kilkenny had the upper hand for the whole game as [[D.J. Carey]] and [[Henry Shefflin]] scored goals for Kilkenny. Clare narrowed Kilkenny's lead in the second half, however, they missed two goal chances. Kilkenny won the title for the 27th time. ==[[Leinster Senior Hurling Championship]]== {{football box | date = April 27
